title: The Judengasse to the Five Arrows: the Court Factor of Hesse and the Sons Sent to Five Capitals
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Sign of the Red Shield

stops.name: Judengasse, Frankfurt: the house called zum roten Schild
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year the house is built; the descent of the sign into a hereditary surname is undated
stops.campa: Isaak Elchanan Bacharach builds a house on the walled Jewish street of Frankfurt and hangs above its door the sign zum roten Schild, at the Red Shield. The gates at either end of the lane are locked at night, on Sundays, and on Christian feast days. Signs serve here as numbers serve elsewhere: a family is known by the painted board over its threshold, and the board outlives the family beneath it. Generations later the descendants of that house carry the sign as a surname into cities where nobody has seen the door: Rothschild. Exactly when the board turned into a name passed down, no source consulted will say.
suggested_refs: The house sign zum roten Schild, Judengasse, Frankfurt, built 1567 by Isaak Elchanan Bacharach

stops.name: Judengasse, Frankfurt: Mayer Amschel is born
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; the day 23 February appears in one lens of the research and is not corroborated in the other
stops.campa: Mayer Amschel is born on the Judengasse to Amschel Moses Rothschild, a currency trader who supplies coins to the Prince of Hesse, and to Schoenche nee Lechnich. The street is a single crowded lane, gated at both ends, among the most tightly packed strips of ground in the Holy Roman Empire; the houses run back deep and narrow because they are not permitted to run wide. The son will not leave this street; his sons will leave it for five capitals. The father's trade is the whole education available on that lane: worn silver, foreign denominations, the weight and fineness of coins struck by princes the family will never see.
suggested_refs: Museum Judengasse, Frankfurt, over the excavated foundations of the ghetto street

stops.name: Fuerth, the yeshiva of David Strauss
stops.date_confidence: contested: German Wikipedia has him entering from 1755, after his father's death; another reading has him there from about 1753 and withdrawn by that death
stops.campa: His father dies in 1755 and his mother the year after. The orphan is sent south to Fuerth, to the Talmudic academy of David Strauss, where a promising boy from a trading house is prepared for the rabbinate. He learns the law of a people forbidden to own land, enter most trades, or sleep a night outside a gate, in a century when the study of money is one of the few things left open to a Jew of Frankfurt. The house in Frankfurt still holds a coin business and no man to run it. He does not stay to be ordained.
suggested_refs: The yeshiva of David Strauss at Fuerth, named in German Wikipedia's account of Rothschild's schooling

stops.name: Hanover, the counting house of Simon Wolf Oppenheimer
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: At thirteen he is apprenticed in Hanover under Jacob Wolf Oppenheimer, at the banking firm of Simon Wolf Oppenheimer, and there learns the machinery a coin stall never shows: bills of exchange, foreign trade, the discounting of paper, the way a debt in one city becomes cash in another with no thaler crossing the road. Hanover keeps no wall around its Jews as Frankfurt does, and its princes come to the firm as clients rather than patrons. He stays six years and goes home in 1763.
suggested_refs: The Oppenheimer banking house at Hanover, where Rothschild served his apprenticeship 1757-1763

stops.name: Judengasse, Frankfurt: back to the coin trade
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He comes home at nineteen and takes up his brothers' business, which is his dead father's business: rare coins, old medals, curiosities, antiquities. It is a trade with an unusual door built into it. A prince who would receive a Jew on no other pretext will receive a dealer carrying a tray of Roman silver, and will talk, and will be flattered, and will want the next thing shown to him first. Mayer Amschel prints catalogues and sends them unbidden to the German courts. He is selling coins and he is buying acquaintance, and only one of the two is priced.
suggested_refs: Rothschild's printed coin and medal catalogues, circulated to German courts in the 1760s

stops.name: Hanau, the petition to Crown Prince Wilhelm
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; the research pool sites the grant at Kassel while Corti's petition is addressed to the Crown Prince at Hanau, where Wilhelm held court until 1785
stops.campa: Crown Prince Wilhelm of Hesse collects coins, and Mayer Amschel has been selling them to him at prices calculated to be remembered. In 1769 he asks for the title that turns a supplier into a servant of the house: Hoffaktor, court factor, court agent. The title carries protection, standing before the city magistrates, and a nail on which an entire career can be hung. The letter is written in a humility so extreme that Corti, reading it a century and a half later, stops to remark on it: he asks only to be, in his own words, most graciously granted the advantage of the appointment.
stops.quote: most graciously be granted the advantage of being appointed court agent
stops.quote_source: Mayer Amschel Rothschild, petition to Crown Prince William of Hanau, 1769, quoted in Egon Caesar Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild, trans. Brian and Beatrix Lunn (1928), p. 8
suggested_refs: Rothschild's 1769 petition for the title of court agent, printed in Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild, p. 8
sources: Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild (1928), p. 8

stops.name: Judengasse, Frankfurt: the marriage to Gutle Schnapper
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On the twenty-ninth of August he marries Gutle Schnapper, daughter of a moneylender of the same street. The marriage does what marriages on the Judengasse do: it ties two trading houses together at the ledger as well as at the canopy. Ten children will come of it, five of them sons. The wife keeps the house, and in the manner of the street the shop is the house; customers are received in the front room and the accounts are kept one wall away from the cooking. She will outlive her husband by thirty-seven years and will never move.
suggested_refs: The Schnapper family of the Judengasse, moneylenders, into which Rothschild married in 1770

stops.name: Kassel, the Hessian soldiers and the English money
stops.date_confidence: traditional: one lens of the research dates Rothschild's share of the subsidy flows to the American war, the other to the years after 1789, and no single transaction is documented
stops.campa: Britain hires Hessian regiments for its American war and pays the Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel for the bodies of his subjects. The money comes back to Germany as bills drawn on London, and bills drawn on London must be discounted, remitted, and turned into coin by somebody. Hesse-Kassel becomes on the strength of it one of the richest treasuries in Europe. Portions of that flow pass through the Frankfurt firm, the largest sums the young dealer has yet been trusted to move.
suggested_refs: The British subsidy treaties for Hessian troops, 1776-1783, and the Kassel treasury they enriched

stops.name: Judengasse 148, the Haus zum Gruenen Schild
stops.date_confidence: contested: German Wikipedia dates the purchase between 1783 and 1787 and the move as either 1786 or 1787, and does not choose
stops.campa: The family leaves the back house called zur Pfanne and takes the Haus zum Gruenen Schild, at the Green Shield, further along the same lane. It is a larger house on the same locked street; the move is a promotion measured in rooms and not in districts. Wilhelm has by now succeeded as Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel, and the business with his treasury has grown past coins into loans, bills, and the management of other men's obligations. He will run the firm out of it for twenty-six years and die in one of its rooms.
suggested_refs: Haus zum Gruenen Schild, Judengasse 148, the family seat from the 1780s to 1849

segments.name: The Ghetto Burns, the Sons Go Out

stops.name: Judengasse, Frankfurt: the French bombardment
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year
stops.campa: French artillery falls on Frankfurt and burns roughly a third of the houses on the Judengasse. The gates that lock the Jews in do nothing to keep shells out. The Rothschild business comes through the fire. Mayer Amschel is fifty-two, the father of five sons, when the war reaches his own door. Families camp in the rubble of a street they are still forbidden to leave, and trading resumes among the burnt frames, because trading is the only permission anyone on the lane holds.
suggested_refs: The 1796 bombardment of Frankfurt and the destruction of a third of the Judengasse

stops.name: Manchester, the third son sent to England
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; the figure of twenty thousand pounds is repeated across the literature without a document behind it
stops.campa: Nathan, twenty-one and the third son, is put on a road out of Germany with capital said to be some twenty thousand pounds and instructions to buy English cloth at its source. This is the first time a son of the Judengasse house is placed permanently in a foreign country, and it is not a branch yet, only a boy with money. He goes to Manchester, where the cloth is made, and buys the dye and the cotton and the finishing as well as the finished piece, taking three profits where an agent takes one. He speaks almost no English and does not wait to learn it.
suggested_refs: Nathan Mayer Rothschild's Manchester textile venture, 1798-1804

stops.name: Kassel, the court factor confirmed
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Thirty-two years after the petition from Hanau, the standing is made formal: Mayer Amschel is Hoffaktor to Wilhelm IX of Hesse-Kassel, court Jew to one of the wealthiest princes in Germany. The firm is no longer selling curiosities to a collector. It issues international loans, moves the Elector's capital, and builds the credit relationships that will let a Frankfurt house place its own sons abroad on its own paper. Everything so far rests on the confidence of a single prince, which is the arrangement that has destroyed court Jews before him.
suggested_refs: The Hoffaktor appointment of 1801 under Wilhelm IX, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel

stops.name: Capel Court, the London Stock Exchange
stops.date_confidence: attested for the start of Stock Exchange dealing; a naturalization commonly dated to the same year is not stated in the cited source
stops.campa: Nathan leaves the cloth trade for the money trade, moves to London, and begins dealing on the Stock Exchange in government securities, at the moment when the British government is about to need every shilling it can raise to fight Napoleon at the far end of Europe. Textiles taught him margins; the funds teach him nerve. Frankfurt now has a son standing inside the deepest capital market in the world. He is short, blunt, and unwelcome in drawing rooms, and none of that counts on a floor where a man is worth only what he can settle.
suggested_refs: Capel Court, seat of the London Stock Exchange, where Nathan Rothschild began dealing in 1804

stops.name: City of London, the banking enterprise begun
stops.date_confidence: attested for the start of the banking enterprise; the New Court lease dates from 1809 and the firm N M Rothschild and Sons from 1811
stops.campa: Nathan begins banking proper: foreign bills, government securities, the discounting of paper drawn between countries at war with one another. The famous address is not his yet. He will take the lease of New Court in St Swithin's Lane four years from now, and the firm will not carry the name N M Rothschild and Sons until 1811. What exists in 1805 is a young man with a book of correspondents, most of them his father and his brothers, writing to him in a Judendeutsch that no clerk in the City can read and no censor can usefully open.
suggested_refs: The founding correspondence of the London house, 1805-1811, held in the Rothschild Archive

stops.name: Kassel, Napoleon's order
stops.date_confidence: attested for the month; Corti dates the order to October 1806
stops.campa: Napoleon writes out the end of the House of Hesse-Cassel in four sentences and sends General Lagrange to carry it out. Treasuries sealed, taxes raised in the Emperor's name, judgments pronounced in the Emperor's name, a dynasty struck off the list of powers. The court factor out of the Frankfurt ghetto is among the very few men in Europe positioned to take custody of a fortune like this one without being searched first. Wilhelm, who has spent forty years accumulating the largest private fortune in Germany, has perhaps hours to decide where it goes.
stops.quote: You will seal up all treasuries and stores and appoint General Lagrange as governor of the country. You will raise taxes and pronounce judgments in my name. Secrecy and speed will be the means through which you will insure complete success. My object is to remove the House of Hesse-Cassel from rulership and to strike it out of the list of powers.
stops.quote_source: Napoleon Bonaparte, order of October 1806, quoted in Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild, trans. Lunn (1928), p. 44
suggested_refs: Napoleon's October 1806 order for the occupation of Hesse-Cassel, printed in Corti, p. 44
sources: Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild (1928), p. 44

stops.name: The Electoral Palace, Kassel: the fortune put out of sight
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the concealment follows the October occupation, and no source reviewed gives a month
stops.campa: The Elector flees north and his property does not travel with him. Chests, plate, securities, and the paper of loans made to half the princes of Europe are moved, concealed, and where concealment fails entered in books that show them as belonging to somebody else, largely in transit, or in London, or set down under a name that is not Wilhelm's. Buderus, the Elector's own financial agent, works with Rothschild rather than around him. French commissioners search Frankfurt houses for the missing Hessian money, this one among them.
suggested_refs: Carl Buderus, the Elector's financial agent, and the concealment of the Hessian fortune in 1806
sources: Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild (1928)

stops.name: Hamburg, the Danish loans
stops.date_confidence: inferred: Corti places the Hamburg journey in the Danish-loan negotiations of 1806 without giving a month
stops.campa: The Elector's money is out on loan to the Danish crown, and Danish business settles in Hamburg. Mayer Amschel goes north himself rather than send a son or a letter, because rival Frankfurt houses are working the same ground and a face is harder to undercut than a quotation. He calls on the bankers, settles the outstanding accounts, and leaves behind him the impression that a man who does what he said he would do on the day he said it is a rarer article in that trade than credit. He is sixty-two and still travelling to win business.
stops.quote: The Crown Agent Rothschild is coming to see me tomorrow in order to settle up our remaining accounts, and he intends to return the day after. It has been a pleasure to me to make the acquaintance of this man, and I shall be glad to be able to do him any service in future.
stops.quote_source: A Hamburg banker, letter to Carl Buderus, quoted in Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild, trans. Lunn (1928), p. 35
suggested_refs: The Danish loans of the Elector of Hesse, settled through Hamburg, in Corti, pp. 35-39
sources: Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild (1928), p. 35

stops.name: Hamburg, the envious may say what they like
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Frankfurt's established banking houses do not enjoy watching a Judengasse coin dealer handle the largest treasury in Germany, and they carry their objections to the Elector's agents. Lawaetz, who has done business with him across the Danish loans, writes to Buderus in his defence on the second of July. The letter claims no genius for him, only that he is a good fellow who deserves respect. The envious, Lawaetz writes, may say what they like against him.
stops.quote: I hope that in the end people will realize that he is a good fellow who deserves to be respected; the envious may say what they like against him.
stops.quote_source: Lawaetz, Hamburg banker, letter to Carl Buderus, 2 July 1806, quoted in Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild, trans. Lunn (1928), p. 44
suggested_refs: Lawaetz's correspondence with Buderus, 1806, on the Frankfurt houses' intrigues against Rothschild
sources: Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild (1928), pp. 39, 44

stops.name: Holstein, the Elector in exile
stops.date_confidence: attested for the exile, which runs to 1813; the routing of the Elector's funds into British operations is tradition
stops.campa: Hesse-Kassel is annexed into Napoleon's new Kingdom of Westphalia, and Wilhelm, now a sovereign without a country, settles under Danish protection in Holstein to wait out the occupation. His capital does not wait with him: it is placed, lent, and invested through Frankfurt and increasingly through London, where his court factor's third son is buying British government paper. The Elector draws his interest and asks few questions about the routes. He comes home in 1813 to find the fortune intact.
suggested_refs: Wilhelm I of Hesse in Danish-held Holstein, 1807-1813

stops.name: Frankfurt, the Wurzach debt
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: A prince owes the exiled Elector money, and the French at Cassel would prefer it never arrived; they offer Rothschild a fifth to a quarter of the sum to divert it to them instead. He declines the cut and arranges a meeting between Buderus and the Wurzach chancellor at a place of his own choosing. Buderus writes to his master on the eighth of March that hope survives at all only through the court agent's efforts. The Elector is a fugitive with no army and no territory; the debt is collected anyway, by two men in a room picked for its discretion.
stops.quote: I owe it entirely to the efforts of the Crown Agent Rothschild that I am still not entirely without hope; and he has undertaken to arrange an interview between myself and the Wurzach chancellor in a place which he will select.
stops.quote_source: Carl Buderus, letter to the Elector of Hesse-Cassel, 8 March 1807, quoted in Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild, trans. Lunn (1928), p. 54
suggested_refs: The debt of Prince von Zeil-Wurzach to the Elector of Hesse, recovered in 1807 through Rothschild
sources: Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild (1928), p. 54

stops.name: Frankfurt, Herr von Goldstein and Arnoldi
stops.date_confidence: inferred: Corti prints the letters as of 1807 without a month
stops.campa: Letters that could hang their writers now travel under invented names. The Elector of Hesse becomes Herr von Goldstein; Rothschild signs himself Arnoldi. Buderus explains to his master why the whole operation must run through a city inside French-controlled Germany rather than around it, and gives the reason in one clause. The Judengasse house is a clearing point for an outlawed sovereign's money, with its ledgers kept in Hebrew characters and a French garrison holding the town outside its gate.
stops.quote: Frankfort is the center point of all my business
stops.quote_source: Carl Buderus, letter to the Elector of Hesse-Cassel, quoted in Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild, trans. Lunn (1928), p. 55
suggested_refs: The Buderus-Rothschild code correspondence, with the Elector as Herr von Goldstein and Rothschild as Arnoldi
sources: Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild (1928), p. 55

stops.name: New Court, St Swithin's Lane: the lease and the bullion
stops.date_confidence: attested for the New Court lease and the turn to bullion; the firm N M Rothschild and Sons is founded in 1811
stops.campa: Nathan takes the lease of New Court in St Swithin's Lane and turns to gold. The arrangement behind the move was drawn up on a locked street in Frankfurt, where the correspondents are brothers and the security for any debt is the family that owes it. Bullion is the one commodity every warring government must have and none can print, and whoever can gather it in London and put it down in Lisbon or Paris or Vienna is selling a service no fleet provides. The house will keep this courtyard for generations.
suggested_refs: New Court, St Swithin's Lane, seat of N M Rothschild and Sons and of the Rothschild Archive

stops.name: Judengasse, Frankfurt: M. A. Rothschild und Soehne
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year
stops.campa: At sixty-six Mayer Amschel makes it formal and takes his three eldest sons into partnership: M. A. Rothschild und Soehne. The name states the design. There is one firm, and it holds sons rather than partners bought in with capital, which means the accounts of one city can be trusted to a man in another with nothing between them by way of enforcement but blood. Nathan in London is not among the three named in the Frankfurt deed. By 1810 he is already the largest limb of the thing, and the deed does not say so.
suggested_refs: The 1810 partnership deed of M. A. Rothschild und Soehne, Frankfurt

stops.name: Frankfurt, the civil rights bought for 440,000 florins
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; the research pool gives no breakdown of the sum and no document
stops.campa: The Grand Duke of Frankfurt sells the Jews of his city their civil rights, and Mayer Amschel finances the purchase: four hundred and forty thousand florins for the standing to live where they choose, to marry without a quota, and to pass through a gate that was locked on them long before he was born. He buys the end of the ghetto and does not use it. He stays in the Green Shield house on the Judengasse until he dies, in a lane that is no longer legally a prison and is still the only address he has ever wanted.
suggested_refs: The 1811 purchase of civil rights for the Jews of Frankfurt from the Grand Duke, financed by Rothschild

stops.name: The Iberian theatre, Wellington's pay
stops.date_confidence: attested for the undertaking; the transfers run through the Peninsular campaigns and beyond
stops.campa: British armies are fighting in Portugal and Spain and cannot be paid in British paper; soldiers on campaign want coin, and Spanish coin at that. The Treasury, which has no other way of doing it, comes to depend on a family firm whose head has never left Frankfurt. Nathan undertakes to move the specie, and to carry as well the subsidies Britain is paying its allies on the continent. Gold is bought in one country, walked or shipped across territory held by the enemy, and produced as cash at a headquarters in the field.
suggested_refs: The specie transfers to Wellington's Peninsular army and the coalition subsidy payments, from 1811

stops.name: Paris, the youngest son sent to buy gold
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; one lens of the research places the move in 1811
stops.campa: Jakob, called James, nineteen years old, is sent to Paris to buy specie and bullion for his brother in London. He is buying gold inside the empire whose armies the gold will be used to fight, under the tacit tolerance of French officials who believe a drain of coin out of Britain can only be weakening it. The last of the five sons is placed. Frankfurt, London, and Paris are held, and Vienna and Naples will follow after their father is dead. He does not live to see the arrangement complete.
suggested_refs: James Mayer de Rothschild's Paris specie operation, 1811-1814

stops.name: The Haus zum Gruenen Schild, the death of Mayer Amschel
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He dies on the nineteenth of September in the house at the Green Shield, sixty-eight years old, on the street where he was born and a few hundred paces from the room where he was born. Better addresses had been available to him for years and he had refused them. His will binds the firm to the male line, keeps the daughters and their husbands out of the books, closes the accounts to outsiders, and instructs his sons to hold together, not one of them yet titled. Five of them are living, and between them they already hold correspondents in every capital at war.
suggested_refs: The will of Mayer Amschel Rothschild, 1812, binding the firm to the male line

stops.name: The Old Jewish Cemetery, Battonnstrasse: the burial
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the burial follows the death of 19 September; no source reviewed gives the day
stops.campa: He is buried in the old Jewish burying ground behind the street, a walled plot first named in a deed of 1300 and closed to new graves in 1828, where his people have been laid for centuries in rows so tight the stones lean against one another. Frankfurt allows its Jews one cemetery as it allows them one street. The man under this stone has just paid for the legal end of both restrictions and lies in the older arrangement. His sons will be buried in London, in Vienna, in Paris, in Naples.
suggested_refs: Alter Juedischer Friedhof, Battonnstrasse, Frankfurt, in use from 1300 to 1828

stops.name: Frankfurt, Amschel keeps the house
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the succession follows the death of September 1812 and no source reviewed dates it
stops.campa: The eldest son takes the founding house and does not move it either. Amschel Mayer keeps M. A. Rothschild und Soehne in Frankfurt, in a firm that has become an international bank while its head office stays a house on a ghetto lane, and Frankfurt keeps the function his father built it for: not the largest of the branches but the hinge, the address the others write to, the clearing point where five sets of books are reconciled and five streams of intelligence arrive first. His mother stays in the rooms above. Exactly when that autumn the succession is settled, no source reviewed says.
suggested_refs: Amschel Mayer Rothschild's stewardship of the Frankfurt house after 1812

stops.name: Waterloo, the news and the legend
stops.date_confidence: attested for the battle; the courier story is tradition and disputed by historians working the Rothschild Archive
stops.campa: Napoleon is beaten in a field south of Brussels and the price of every government bond in Europe moves that week. Tradition holds that the family's own couriers put the outcome into Nathan's hands before the official despatch reached London, and that he traded on it. Wellington wrote the despatch on the nineteenth; it reached Lord Bathurst on the evening of the twenty-first. The certain part is duller. The wars that made this family are over, and the debt they were financed with will be refinanced for the next thirty years.
suggested_refs: Brian Cathcart on the arrival of the Waterloo despatch in London, 21 June 1815

stops.name: Vienna, the arms submitted to the Heralds' College
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year
stops.campa: Salomon, the second son, submits a design to the Austrian Heralds' College on behalf of his brothers: a quartered shield, and in the fourth quarter an arm gripping five arrows, one for each of the five brothers, a symbol, as he writes, of their unity. Nathan in London is not yet ennobled and therefore cannot be counted among them. The College reviews the submitted design carefully and approves the arms with only four arrows in the quarter instead of the five requested.
stops.quote: fourth quarter, azure, an arm bearing five arrows (a symbol of the unity of the five brothers)
stops.quote_source: Salomon Mayer Rothschild, letter describing the family's proposed coat of arms, 1816, quoted in Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild, trans. Lunn (1928), p. 179
suggested_refs: The Austrian Heralds' College file on the Rothschild arms, 1816, in Corti, pp. 179-180
sources: Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild (1928), p. 179

stops.name: Vienna, the patent of nobility
stops.date_confidence: contested: 1817 is the date usually given, while the Rothschild family article has four sons ennobled in 1816 and Nathan in 1818
stops.campa: Emperor Francis I ennobles the sons of a man five years dead, for a loan carried through meticulously and punctually: the English subsidy transactions of 1815. The College notes in its file that caution is needed with members of the Jewish nation, who are unfamiliar with the prerogatives of nobility. Count Stadion, drafting the patent, advises that it should not enter into details of the services rendered but state the matter generally: the brothers, he writes, have shown an exceptional readiness to render services outside their actual duties.
stops.quote: since the two brothers Meyer Amschel [sic] Rothschild and Solomon Meyer Rothschild have carried through a loan most meticulously and punctually...and have also shown an exceptional readiness to render services outside their actual duties, his Majesty has been most graciously moved, etc., etc.
stops.quote_source: Count Stadion to Chancellor Ugarte, on the drafting of the Rothschild patent of nobility, quoted in Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild, trans. Lunn (1928), p. 179
suggested_refs: The Rothschild patents of nobility, Vienna, and the Heralds' College memorandum, Corti pp. 179-180
sources: Corti, The Rise of the House of Rothschild (1928), pp. 179-180

stops.name: Rue Laffitte, Paris: de Rothschild Freres
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year
stops.campa: James turns a wartime specie operation into a standing bank and opens de Rothschild Freres. Within six years the house is banker to the French government, the state whose armies his gold helped to defeat. The youngest son of the Judengasse becomes the richest man in France. He buys the Hotel de Saint-Florentin in 1838, and bank and house descend together through the family to his great-granddaughter Bethsabee de Rothschild, whose father inherits both in 1905.
suggested_refs: De Rothschild Freres, rue Laffitte, and the Hotel de Saint-Florentin, Paris

stops.name: Vienna, S M von Rothschild
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year
stops.campa: Salomon is sent to Austria to make permanent what had been a run of separate transactions, and founds S M von Rothschild in Vienna. He becomes banker to Metternich's state, lending to the empire that polices the settlement his family's loans helped pay for. Vienna is the city where the court Jew was invented as an office and where the office was periodically destroyed along with its holder. Salomon lends to this treasury rather than serving it, and four brothers hold the same standing in four other capitals, so no single sovereign can seize the whole.
suggested_refs: S M von Rothschild, Vienna, and its financing of the Kaiser Ferdinands-Nordbahn from 1836

stops.name: Naples, C. M. de Rothschild e Figli
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year
stops.campa: Austrian troops occupy the Kingdom of Naples to put down its revolution, and the occupation has to be paid for. Carl, the fourth son, is sent south and stays, founding C. M. de Rothschild e Figli and becoming the dominant bank to the Bourbon crown. The fifth arrow is in place. Between Naples, Frankfurt, Vienna, Paris, and London the couriers now run on a private schedule faster than the posts of the governments they serve. Carl's branch will be the first to close, in 1861, its assets folded back into his father's house.
suggested_refs: C. M. de Rothschild e Figli, Naples, 1821-1861

stops.name: Vienna, the barony and the five arrows
stops.date_confidence: attested; one lens of the research misdates the arms to the 1817 ennoblement, and the correction to 1822 is followed here
stops.campa: On the twenty-ninth of September the five brothers are raised to the hereditary barony, and this time the arms come with the title: the clenched fist gripping five arrows, and beneath the shield the words Concordia, Integritas, Industria. Tradition reads the arrows out of the Psalm in which the sons of a man's youth are as arrows in the hand of a warrior, and calls the design a blessing spoken by the father before he scattered them. He left no such blessing on paper. What he left was the arrangement the emblem describes.
suggested_refs: The Freiherr diploma of 29 September 1822 and the five-arrows arms with the motto Concordia, Integritas, Industria

stops.name: Threadneedle Street, the Bank of England relieved
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; the panic runs through the winter of 1825 and the month is not specified in the sources reviewed
stops.campa: A panic runs through the London banks and the Bank of England comes near the bottom of its reserve. Nathan supplies coin and bullion in quantity enough to carry it through. The institution that would have discounted nothing for this family a generation earlier is kept standing by a Frankfurt ghetto house's stock of gold. It is December 1825 now, thirteen years after his father's death and twenty-seven years after he was sent abroad with cloth money.
suggested_refs: The banking crisis of 1825 and Nathan Rothschild's bullion supply to the Bank of England

stops.name: Frankfurt, the death of Nathan
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Nathan comes back to Frankfurt for the wedding of his son Lionel and does not leave it alive. The last weeks of his life are spent at that family wedding, in the town his father never left. He had made the London house the centre of gravity of the whole network and had run it as his father ran the Judengasse shop: by letter, by family, and by declining to explain himself to anyone outside it. An abscess turns septic, and the largest banker in London dies aged fifty-eight, on 28 July 1836.
suggested_refs: The wedding of Lionel de Rothschild at Frankfurt, June 1836, and Nathan's final illness

stops.name: Brady Street, Whitechapel: the funeral
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The body is brought from Frankfurt to London and buried on the eighth of August in the Jewish ground at Brady Street in Whitechapel. The procession draws crowds the length of the City. Forty years earlier no member of this family could sleep a night outside a locked lane in Frankfurt, and the gate was still bolted at dusk. He is laid in an East End burial ground among Jews of no fortune whatever, which is what the law of his people prescribes and what his money did not alter.
suggested_refs: Brady Street Cemetery, Whitechapel, burial place of Nathan Mayer Rothschild

stops.name: Paris, the pamphlet that invented the legend
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of publication
stops.campa: A pamphlet appears in Paris under the pseudonym Satan, written by Georges Marie Mathieu-Dairnvaell, titled the edifying and curious history of Rothschild the First, King of the Jews. It is where the Waterloo story starts: not in 1815, not in any newspaper of that summer, but thirty-one years afterwards, in a libel. John Reeves repeats it in an 1887 house history, Frederic Morton in the next century, Hollywood films it in 1934. The sentence most often put into Mayer Amschel's mouth is of the same manufacture and no document carries it.
stops.quote: Let me issue and control a nation's money and I care not who makes its laws
stops.quote_source: Widely attributed to Mayer Amschel Rothschild since at least the early twentieth century; no primary document, letter, or contemporary record has ever been produced, and no biographer with archival access traces it to any Rothschild source
suggested_refs: Georges Marie Mathieu-Dairnvaell, Histoire edifiante et curieuse de Rothschild Ier, roi des Juifs (Paris, 1846)
sources: English Wikipedia, citing the 1846 Mathieu-Dairnvaell pamphlet

stops.name: The Haus zum Gruenen Schild, Gutle to the end
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of death; the day is not given in the material reviewed
stops.campa: Gutle Rothschild dies in the Green Shield house at ninety-six, having lived in it since the move of the seventeen-eighties and refused to leave it after her sons were made barons of the Austrian Empire. Her sons are creditors to five governments. The Judengasse is being demolished around her by degrees, and she outlives most of it. She keeps to the end the same house, the same lane, the same neighbours, and the same three rooms she kept when her husband was selling medals out of the front one.
suggested_refs: Gutle Rothschild in the Haus zum Gruenen Schild, 1786-1849

stops.name: New Court, the diamonds of Kimberley
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of the De Beers amalgamation finance; the month follows the corpus record of the negotiation
stops.campa: Seventy-five years after Mayer Amschel's death, Cecil Rhodes climbs the steps at New Court to ask N M Rothschild and Sons for the money to amalgamate the diamond mines of Kimberley into De Beers. Mayer Amschel lent to princes who could grant a Jew a court title and little else; his descendants lend to a company that will govern territory. The house Nathan founded is underwriting the conquest of a continent. Rhodes gets the money, and afterwards a chartered company besides.
suggested_refs: The 1887 De Beers amalgamation and its financing through N M Rothschild and Sons

stops.name: The Old Jewish Cemetery, the stone found again
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of rediscovery
stops.campa: The cemetery is wrecked in the Nazi years and the Judengasse itself is gone, cleared and built over. In 1968 the original gravestone of Mayer Amschel Rothschild is found and set up again in the Ehrenhain, the grove of honour, among the salvaged stones. The inscription is transcribed and catalogued in an epigraphy database. Where exactly the stone was for the century and a half in between, toppled, buried, or carried off, no source reviewed will say.
suggested_refs: The Steinheim Institute epigraphy database entry for Mayer Amschel Rothschild's gravestone

stops.name: Battonnstrasse 47, the street excavated
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 2016 redesign; the museum's opening year, generally given as 1992, was not established with certainty in the material reviewed
stops.campa: City construction work in 1987 turns up the foundations of five houses of the Judengasse, and a museum is built over them at Battonnstrasse 47, beside the cemetery. The Green Shield house itself is not among the five foundations uncovered. Visitors walk below street level along the excavated line of the lane: the ritual bath, the wells, the cramped back rooms, the drainage of a street that held a few thousand people in a space meant for a few hundred.
suggested_refs: Museum Judengasse, Battonnstrasse 47, Frankfurt, over the excavated ghetto foundations
sources: Juedisches Museum Frankfurt, Museum Judengasse visitor page
